cards.text: Jesus is still talking to His disciples, and now He tells them, 'Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.' Apron on, lights on, and NOBODY is hitting snooze.

cards.question: Jesus says His disciples should be like servants who are waiting up for someone. Who are those servants waiting for?
The master is coming back from a wedding banquet. When he comes and knocks, the servants who are ready can open the door for him at ___.

cards.text: The master gets home, finds his servants on watch, and Jesus calls those servants blessed. Then Jesus tells what the master does next, and friend, hold on to your apron.

cards.question: The master gets home and finds his servants on watch. What does he do for them?

answers.text: He waits on them at the table
He gives each one a bag of silver
He lets them sleep until morning

cards.question: The master might come late, in the second or third watch of the night. Even then, the servants he finds alert are still blessed.

cards.text: Then Jesus switches pictures. Now it's a homeowner, and a thief who's coming to break in, and let me tell you, friend, no thief in history has ever sent a calendar invite that says 'Break-in, 2 AM, please confirm.'

cards.question: Jesus says that even if the homeowner had known the hour the thief was coming, he still couldn't have stopped the break-in.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings it all home with the Son of Man, a name Jesus uses for Himself (Luke 9:22). Sit up straight for this one, friend, because I am, and I don't even HAVE a back.

cards.question: Jesus says, 'You also must be ___, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not ___.'

cards.text: Peter, one of Jesus's disciples (Luke 6:13-14), has a question about the parable. Every meeting needs one person brave enough to unmute, and today that's Peter.

cards.question: What does Peter want to know about the parable Jesus just told?

answers.text: Whether it's for them or everyone
When the master will come back
Which servant the master will reward

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question of His own: who then is the faithful and wise manager the master puts in charge of his servants? Friend, if somebody asked me that, I'd be pointing my whole mustache at myself going ME, it's ME, pick ME.

cards.question: The master puts a faithful and wise manager in charge of his servants. What's the manager's job?

answers.text: Give them their portion on time
Keep count of the master's flocks

cards.question: When the master returns and finds the faithful and wise manager doing his job, he puts him in charge of all his possessions.

cards.text: But suppose that same manager says something in his heart about when his master is coming back. Uh oh.

cards.question: Suppose the manager the master put in charge says something in his heart about when his master is coming back. What does he say?

answers.text: His master will be a long time coming
His master will be home before dawn
His master will send a messenger first

cards.text: Then that manager begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.

cards.question: The master of the manager who began beating the servants comes back on a day and at an hour that manager expects.

cards.text: When the master comes, he cuts that servant to pieces and assigns him a place with the unbelievers. That's a heavy line, friend.

Then Jesus compares two servants: one knows his master's will but doesn't get ready or follow his instructions, and the other unknowingly does things worthy of punishment. One read the memo, and one never got the memo.

cards.question: The servant who knew his master's will gets fewer blows than the servant who didn't know.
Jesus says that from everyone who has been given a great deal, ___ will be required.

cards.text: And from the one entrusted with much, even more will be demanded, so a guy handed a whole planet of ovens takes that line VERY personally. Stick around, friend, because Jesus isn't done teaching yet.
